clue.text: Expression of Persian origin

parts.note: the 'expression' is not a phrase from Iran but the sound uttered by a Persian cat

explanation.surface: A linguist traces a saying back to ancient Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: Persian looks like a language or nationality; here it is the long-haired breed of cat, and its expression is the noise it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry a cat makes is its call, so a Persian cat's utterance is this sound.

clue.text: Time to change lodgings and take another job

definitions.meaning: a ... flit is a secret night-time move to dodge the rent, done by the light of the moon
to work a second job on the side

explanation.surface: A good moment to move house and start a second job.
explanation.walkthrough: The British 'moonlight flit' is slipping away at night without paying rent; the second sense is holding a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the hour of a secret flit from rented rooms, and the verb means working a second job.

clue.text: Warning to set out later

indicators.note: to set out means to arrange the letters afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A notice that you should start your journey later.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm or signal that tells people to be on guard is a warning.

clue.text: Finished — not going back to sea

definitions.meaning: done for, a spent force
cast ashore by the waves and left stranded

explanation.surface: Retired, and never returning to the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone done for is like flotsam thrown up on the beach, never to float again.

clue.text: Art to some small degree outstanding

definitions.text: Art to some small degree outstanding

parts.words: Art to some small degree outstanding
parts.note: outstanding is read literally as standing out from a surface: sculpture whose figures project only slightly

explanation.surface: A critic gives a lukewarm verdict on some artwork as only slightly excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to praise; in fact it means physically projecting, and this sculpture projects only a little from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Low relief is carving in which the figures project only slightly from the flat background.

clue.text: Prejudice evident in getting at Jack

definitions.meaning: a leaning or partiality
in lawn bowls the weighting of a bowl makes it curve as it travels towards the jack, the small target ball

explanation.surface: Bigotry shows when people pick on Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls the jack is the small white target ball, and each bowl is weighted to curve as it rolls towards it. 'Getting at' suggests nagging; here it means reaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning in judgement is prejudice, and a bowl's weighted curve is the same word.

clue.text: Fascinated by description of the sleeping beauty

definitions.meaning: held entranced
the princess of the fairy tale lies bound under an enchantment

explanation.surface: Enthralled by an account of the fairy-tale princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entranced is like being held by magic, as the fairy-tale princess was by a curse.

clue.text: Beauty's —— yet Is crimson in thy lips" (R & J)

definitions.text: Beauty's —— yet Is crimson in thy lips" (R & J)

parts.words: Beauty's —— yet Is crimson in thy lips" (R & J)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Romeo's speech over Juliet in the tomb, where the missing word is a flag

explanation.surface: A line from Romeo and Juliet with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo, in the tomb, says that beauty's flag still flies crimson in Juliet's lips and cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a banner, the flag that beauty still flies in Juliet's red lips.

clue.text: Puck is a fast mover in this play

definitions.text: Puck is a fast mover in this play

parts.words: Puck is a fast mover in this play
parts.note: Puck seems to be the sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream, but here is a rubber disc, and play means a sport

explanation.surface: In Shakespeare's comedy Puck darts swiftly about.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck evokes Shakespeare's sprite who girdles the earth in forty minutes; the play is a game on a rink.
explanation.definitionFit: This rink sport is played by skaters striking a rubber disc that travels very fast.

clue.text: Power of the long arm ?

definitions.meaning: strength or energy
the long arm of the law is the police

explanation.surface: Asks how far the police's reach extends.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is power, and the police, the law's long arm, are the constabulary of that name.

clue.text: Represent too strongly the Governor's position

definitions.meaning: to exaggerate or overplay something
a governor ranks above the region he governs, so his place is literally above the territory

explanation.surface: Someone overplays the powers attached to a colonial governor's post.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate is to put things too high, and a governor sits literally above the territory he runs.

clue.text: Stick by the side of Adam

definitions.meaning: to stick is to pierce, as with a lance
the ... side is an old term for the male line of a family, Adam standing for men

explanation.surface: Stay loyal beside the first man in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The spear side' (as opposed to the distaff side) is the male line of descent; the clue suggests Adam's rib instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick is to pierce with a lance-like weapon, and the male line is called the spear side.

clue.text: Make untidy bed

definitions.meaning: to strew rubbish about
straw or bedding laid down for animals, or a stretcher for carrying a person

explanation.surface: Mess up the bed you have just made.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter rubbish is to make a place untidy, and straw bedding for animals has the same name.

clue.text: Staff helping to set a high standard

definitions.text: Staff helping to set a high standard

parts.words: Staff helping to set a high standard
parts.note: staff is a pole, not employees, and a standard is a flag hoisted high rather than a level of quality

explanation.surface: Office workers help to raise the bar of quality.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff suggests employees and a high standard excellence; read as a pole and a banner the clue describes what a flag flies from.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall mast is the staff from which a banner, or standard, is flown aloft.

clue.text: Followed by kingfisher — to take the drag out of flying!

definitions.text: Followed by kingfisher — to take the drag out of flying!

parts.words: Followed by kingfisher — to take the drag out of flying!
parts.note: a kingfisher follows the course of a brook, and to shape something so air resistance is reduced is the verb

explanation.surface: A kingfisher's flight path explains how to cut air resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A kingfisher flies along the line of a brook; the word also means shaping an aircraft to reduce drag.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaping a body smoothly so air resistance is lessened; the bird darts along a brook's course.

clue.text: Get a guard into trouble passing out

indicators.note: trouble stirs up and disturbs the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Get a sentry into hot water while he is leaving the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing out' sounds like fainting; it is the ceremony at which cadets finish training.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing-out parade marks cadets completing their course, the military equivalent of finishing a degree.

clue.text: Disabuse us as to her writing ability

definitions.text: Disabuse us as to her writing ability

indicators.note: disabuse is read as abuse, maltreat, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Set us straight about how well she writes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disabuse' scrambles US AS TO HER; the clue also challenges doubts about a woman writer's ability.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a female writer, one who has proved her ability with a pen.

clue.text: Leave out the captain

definitions.meaning: to omit or pass over
short for skipper, the leader of a team, as in curling or bowls

explanation.surface: Drop the team leader from the side.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to pass over it, and a team's leader is its skipper, shortened.

clue.text: Straw bed for friendly sounding donkey

annotationWithheld.why: Straw bed for friendly sounding donkey: PALLY + ASS said aloud gives PALLIASSE, but the indicator 'sounding' stands between the two words said aloud, so no single heard leaf can be quoted
annotationWithheld.clue: Straw bed for friendly sounding donkey

clue.text: Turn liar perhaps as an experiment

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Try turning into a liar just to see what happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or test run before the real thing is an experiment.

clue.text: Poet Laureate's Gallery

definitions.meaning: Nahum ... was Poet Laureate from 1692
the London art museum founded by Henry ...

explanation.surface: An art gallery named after the official national poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Nahum Tate held the Laureateship in the 1690s; the London galleries bear the name of the sugar magnate Henry Tate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum Tate was a seventeenth-century court poet, and the London art museums share that surname.

clue.text: Mint issue of the Queen's coin

definitions.meaning: a herb of the mint family
a royal penny, the small coin issued by the monarch

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint releases one of the monarch's coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the place where coins are made, matching the surface; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb belongs to the mint family, and read as two words it is a sovereign's small coin.

clue.text: Stupid chap, that one, to invest in textiles

parts.note: a clot is a stupid person
he, that one, a male person

explanation.surface: A foolish man puts his money into the cloth trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial; it means to dress or robe someone, here in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone in robes is to dress them in fabric, an old sense of the verb.

clue.text: It helps to remove a coat when hot

definitions.text: It helps to remove a coat when hot

parts.words: It helps to remove a coat when hot
parts.note: the coat is a layer of paint stripped off with a heated tool, not a garment shed on a warm day

explanation.surface: Something that helps you take off your jacket once the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is paint, and a decorator's flame tool softens it so it can be scraped away.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch that throws a hot flame is used by decorators to soften and strip old paint.

clue.text: Common cleaner

definitions.meaning: the yellow-flowered shrub that grows on heaths and commons
a long-handled brush for sweeping

explanation.surface: An everyday household cleaning tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow shrub of the heath grows on common land, and the sweeping brush is named after it.

clue.text: Far as one possibly goes in Africa

definitions.text: Far as one possibly goes in Africa

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: As far as a person might travel across Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges FARAS with I (one); the whole clue also describes an expedition in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition in Africa to watch or hunt wildlife, a long trek into the bush.

clue.text: Correct the last word before day-break?

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
the break, or beginning, of day is its first letter D

explanation.surface: Fix the final word before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day-break' looks like dawn; it is the start of the word day.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a text is to alter it so it is right.

clue.text: A little cricket, and this in Hampshire

definitions.meaning: a short spell of six balls in cricket
placed after the word and, this word makes a Hampshire town

explanation.surface: A short burst of cricket played in a Hampshire village.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six balls bowled from one end. 'And this in Hampshire' says AND plus the answer makes a Hampshire town, Andover.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a set of six deliveries is a small portion of play.

clue.text: Public sort of square by 25

parts.note: 25-down is the over of cricket, here placed after the T-square letter's partner
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler, so a T is a sort of square

explanation.surface: A public type of town square beside another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By 25' means put beside the answer to 25-down, OVER; the T comes from a T-square, a drawing instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly in plain view is public rather than hidden.

clue.text: Cape Town, GB

definitions.meaning: an ... cape is a sleeveless cloak
a town in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: Cape Town is placed in Great Britain by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the South African city; split it into a cloak and a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland cloak is named after this Scottish town, the capital of the Highlands.

clue.text: Literally a shot may come from one

definitions.text: Literally a shot may come from one

parts.words: Literally a shot may come from one
parts.note: a shot, taken literally as a firing rather than a drink or attempt, comes from a soldier armed with a firearm

explanation.surface: A remark that a 'shot', in the literal sense, can come from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier carries an old smooth-bore gun, so a literal shot can come from him; Dumas's heroes come to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An infantryman armed with an early smooth-bore gun fires shots in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Dug-out in the north-east somewhat poky

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the compass letters

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

indicators.note: out signals the letters of dug are put out of order

explanation.surface: A trench dug in northeast England is a little cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dug-out' looks like a trench, but 'out' is the anagram signal on dug and 'in' the container signal. 'Poky' is read as poking a little rather than cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod with the elbow is a slight poke, so the clue treats it as mildly poking.
